title: Session teardown resets and stops every associated stream regardless of which half this endpoint owns
evidence: terminateAssociatedStreams appends both streamResetFrames.append(stream.reset(...)) and streamStopSendingFrames.append(stream.stopSending(...)) for every id in streamIDsBySessionID/bufferedStreamIDsBySessionID (WebTransportSession.swift:1435-1457); the set includes peer-initiated unidirectional streams registered by acceptUnidirectionalStreamWithActions (WebTransportSession.swift:985-987) and locally initiated unidirectional streams (WebTransportSession.swift:865). QUICStreamState.reset/stopSending (QUICCoreState.swift:706-716) bypass the ensureCanSend/ensureCanReceive direction guards (QUICCoreState.swift:718-733). RFC 9000 section 19.4/19.5 require STREAM_STATE_ERROR for a RESET_STREAM on a send-only stream or a STOP_SENDING on a receive-only stream. The sibling C99 implementation guards exactly this: C99/src/http3/driver.c:917-929 defines has_send_half/has_receive_half and 979-998 gates reset/stop_sending on them. Reachable through the shipped WebTransportHTTP3Core library product; the top-level runtime discards the frames (WebTransportInteroperableNetworkRuntime.swift:763-769).
expected: Emit RESET_STREAM only on a stream whose send half this endpoint owns and STOP_SENDING only where it owns the receive half (both halves for bidirectional streams).

title: Short-header reserved bits are never validated, although the long-header and Retry decoders do validate them
evidence: QUICShortHeaderPacket.decode checks only (first & 0x80) == 0 and (first & 0x40) != 0 (QUICPacket.swift:303-308) before reading the packet number; the long-header decoder rejects (first & 0x0c) != 0 (QUICPacket.swift:90-94) and Retry does the same (:214-216). grep -n "0x18" WebTransportQUICCore/QUICPacket.swift returns no match. RFC 9001 section 5.4 requires PROTOCOL_VIOLATION for non-zero reserved bits after header protection removal; short-header reserved bits are 0x18. C99 checks both forms: C99/src/quic/packet.c:286 (0x0c) and 404-406 (0x18), escalated in C99/src/quic/packet_io.c:218-221. Public API of the shipped WebTransportQUICCore product.
expected: Reject a short-header packet whose reserved bits (0x18) are non-zero with QUICCodecError.malformed, matching the long-header path.

title: Per-connection inbound-stream queue has no bound and post-establishment unidirectional streams have no consumer
evidence: InteroperableQUICStreamQueue has private var queued: [Int: [Element]] = [:] (:2330) and appends every inbound stream with queued[direction, default: []].append(stream) (:2390) with no cap and no eviction; fail(_:) only resumes waiters (:2441-2450). The only consumers are acceptBidirectionalStream (:602), the server's CONNECT stream (:1447) and readPeerControlStream during establishment (:1890). WebTransportSessionManager.acceptUnidirectionalStream (WebTransportHTTP3Core/WebTransportSession.swift:949) has no caller anywhere in WebTransportNetworkRuntime or WebTransport (grep: no matches), and the public API only exposes acceptBidirectionalStream (WebTransport/WebTransport.swift:314-320). QUIC stream limits do not bound this over time because RFC 9000 section 4.6 stops counting a stream once it is closed regardless of application reads; the exact remote growth rate depends on Network.framework stream accounting, hence suspected.
expected: A bounded per-direction stream queue (cap plus reset/refusal of excess streams) and a consumer for peer-initiated unidirectional streams, so no accepted stream is retained for the life of the connection without bound.

title: Both final-size checks in QUICStreamState.receive are unreachable, so FINAL_SIZE_ERROR is never produced by this type
evidence: receive() calls ensureCanReceive() first (:664), which throws when receiveClosed or stopSendingSent is set (:727-734); finalReceiveSize is private(set) and assigned exactly once in the file, at :688 together with receiveClosed = true. Therefore both `if let finalReceiveSize` tests (:679, :685) always see nil. grep -n finalReceiveSize QUICCoreState.swift shows the declaration at :614, reads at :679/:685 and the single assignment at :688. TLSQUICConnectionState compensates with its own pre-check (TLSQUICConnectionState.swift:338-361), which is evidence the intended check is misplaced.
expected: A STREAM frame whose offset+length exceeds a known final size, and a FIN whose size differs from one already recorded, are reported as final-size errors; finalReceiveSize is also recorded from RESET_STREAM (RFC 9000 sections 4.5, 19.4).

title: HTTP field values from the peer are never validated: CR, LF and NUL are accepted, and :status accepts non-3DIGIT forms
evidence: HTTPFieldLine.init validates only the name and stores the value verbatim (QPACK.swift:8-25); decodeStringLiteral stops at `guard let value = String(data: decodedBytes, encoding: .utf8)` (QPACK.swift:866-880), and "\r\n", "\u{0}" and other C0 controls are valid UTF-8. RFC 9110 section 5.5 forbids CR/LF/NUL in field values and RFC 9114 section 4.1.2 makes such a field section malformed. Separately, WebTransportSessionHeaders.status uses UInt16(statusValue) plus a 100...599 range check (WebTransportSession.swift:1727-1735) and WebTransportHTTP3Headers.validateSuccessfulResponse uses Int(status) (WebTransportHeaders.swift:59-64); `swift -e 'print(UInt16("+200") as Any, UInt16("0200") as Any)'` prints Optional(200) Optional(200), so :status "+200"/"0200" is accepted although RFC 9110 section 15 defines status-code as 3DIGIT.
expected: Reject field values containing C0 controls, DEL, CR, LF or NUL, and accept :status only as exactly three ASCII digits before converting.

title: CryptoApple HKDF-Expand-Label silently wraps the RFC 5869 block counter, while the TLSCore copy is guarded against it
evidence: hkdfExpandLabel guards only outputByteCount <= UInt16.max (QUICInitialKeyDerivation.swift:61-64) and hkdfExpand increments `var counter: UInt8` with `counter &+= 1` and no block-count cap (:81-102); TLS13KeySchedule.hkdfExpandLabel has `guard outputByteCount <= 255 * sha256Length` with a comment naming the counter-wrap hazard (TLS13KeySchedule.swift:36-44). Probe of the copied function: outputByteCount = 255*32 gives blocks=255 counter wrapped to 0: false; outputByteCount = 255*32 + 32 gives blocks=256 counter wrapped to 0: true. QUICPacketProtection.deriveKeys (WebTransportCryptoApple/QUICPacketProtection.swift:19-42) is public and forwards caller byte counts here. Not peer-controlled on the shipped runtime path.
expected: Reject outputByteCount above 255 * 32 (the SHA-256 RFC 5869 limit) instead of silently producing a non-RFC HKDF stream.

title: Pinned-certificate trust policy and CertificateVerify verifier are unreachable from any shipped client path
evidence: grep -rn "TLSPinnedCertificateTrustPolicy|TLSCertificateVerifier|evaluate(certificateChainDER" Swift/Sources returns only the definitions (TLSIdentityTrust.swift:123/138/154, TLSCertificateVerification.swift:19) and one conformance use (WebTransportCLIConformance.swift:732-733). WebTransportQUICPeerTrustPolicy offers only .systemTrust and .localDevelopmentSelfSigned (WebTransportInteroperableNetworkRuntime.swift:48-85), so the shipped runtime delegates all validation to Network.framework and cannot pin a leaf certificate. WebTransportComplianceMatrix.swift:67-78 claims "pinned trust" as implemented.
expected: Either expose pinning as a client trust-policy configuration wired into the Network.framework verify path, or state that pinning is a WebTransportTLSCore-only API and correct the compliance-matrix claim.

title: CRYPTO-stream reassembly is quadratic in the buffered byte count and retains every consumed byte forever
evidence: append() calls pendingByteCount once per frame (TLSHandshakeFlight.swift:132) and recomputePendingByteCount does two full passes over bytesByOffset (:106-116), so a peer feeding one-byte CRYPTO frames costs O(n^2) (~2x10^9 dictionary probes at the 64 KiB ceiling set at :61) before authentication; bytesByOffset is one dictionary entry per byte (:63, :147). Consumed bytes are never removed (deliberate, :66-73) and every decoded message is appended to the transcript (:218, TLS13KeySchedule.swift:141-143) with no state machine rejecting repeated handshake messages (TLSQUICConnectionState.swift:132-140), so repeated well-formed handshake messages grow both structures without bound for the connection lifetime. Reachable only through the shipped WebTransportTLSCore library product; Network.framework terminates TLS in the runtime.
expected: Pending-byte accounting is O(1) per append (stored counter updated by append/markConsumed), and total retained CRYPTO/transcript bytes are bounded for a long-lived connection.

title: Peer-controlled echo text is printed into operator logs without escaping (log injection)
evidence: WebTransportServer/main.swift:51-53 prints message="\(result.message)" and WebTransportClient/main.swift:34-36 prints the same shape; result.message is the peer's payload decoded as UTF-8 (WebTransportInteroperableNetworkRuntime.swift:1321-1327 from echoOneStream :1349-1358 for the server, and :365-377 for the client). A peer can embed a double quote and newlines to forge additional log lines. The redacted WebTransportLogEvent path (WebTransport/WebTransport.swift:119-147) and WebTransportErrorSurface (:167-215) exist precisely to keep peer text out of output; these two CLI printfs bypass them.
expected: Never interpolate peer-derived text raw; print its byte count (as WebTransportLogEvent.sessionClosed(reasonByteCount:) does) or sanitize control characters first.

title: parseKeyType maps the Ed25519 key type name to kSecAttrKeyTypeECSECPrimeRandom
evidence: Phase11IdentitySupport.parseKeyType returns kSecAttrKeyTypeECSECPrimeRandom for both "ec"/"p256" and "ed25519" (Phase11Identity.swift:92-101). A caller selecting ed25519 therefore builds the wrong SecKey attributes (OSStatus -50 on the P-256 attempt, or a mislabelled identity if a P-256 blob is supplied) instead of being told the key type is unsupported. The target is imported by a shipped executable (LibrarySmokeServer/main.swift:4).
expected: "ed25519" is either mapped to the correct Ed25519 key type or rejected with the same unsupported-key-type error as any unknown name.

title: Error-code selection is decided by substring-matching a human-readable message
evidence: closeDueToStreamError switches on `case .streamStateViolation(let message) where message.contains("final size")` to choose FINAL_SIZE_ERROR versus STREAM_STATE_ERROR (TLSQUICConnectionState.swift:325-335). The two cases are distinguishable only by the prose thrown at QUICCoreState.swift:680 and :686, and per F-swift-line-security-04 neither message can currently be produced. Any wording change silently reclassifies a wire-visible connection error.
expected: A dedicated QUICStateError case (for example finalSizeViolation) matched structurally rather than by message text.

title: setsockopt failure is ignored
evidence: QUICUDPPort.init calls `unsafe setsockopt(fd, SOL_SOCKET, SO_REUSEADDR, &reuse, socklen_t(MemoryLayout<Int32>.size))` and discards the result (QUICUDPPort.swift:59-62), while bind (:70-77), getsockname (:85-92), sendto (:115-125), poll (:149-155) and recvmsg (:184-187) all check their status and throw QUICUDPError.posix after close(fd).
expected: Check the setsockopt status and throw QUICUDPError.posix(operation: "setsockopt", code: errno) after close(fd), like the neighbouring syscall wrappers.
